Unit 1 of 10: Eukaryotic Cells and Organelles

Key ideas

  • Organelles and functions:
  • nucleus: contains chromosomes (DNA); nucleolus makes ribosomes; double-membrane envelope with pores;
  • rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER): ribosomes on the surface; makes and transports proteins;
  • smooth ER (SER): makes lipids and steroids;
  • Golgi body (apparatus): modifies proteins (for example adds sugars) and packages them in vesicles;
  • mitochondria: site of aerobic respiration (ATP production); double membrane with cristae; contain 70S ribosomes and circular DNA;
  • ribosomes: 80S in the cytoplasm (protein synthesis);
  • lysosomes: contain hydrolytic enzymes;
  • centrioles: in animal cells; involved in spindle formation;
  • chloroplasts (plants): photosynthesis; double membrane, thylakoids (grana), stroma, 70S ribosomes, circular DNA;
  • cell wall (plants): cellulose; prevents bursting;
  • large permanent vacuole (plants): contains cell sap, maintains turgor;
  • plasmodesmata: cytoplasmic links between plant cells;
  • microvilli: folds of the cell surface membrane increasing surface area;
  • cilia: for movement of fluids (made of microtubules).
  • ATP is the universal energy currency, made in mitochondria (and chloroplasts) and used throughout the cell.

Worked examples

Example 1: a cell secreting digestive enzymes has lots of RER, Golgi bodies and mitochondria.

Example 2: a structure with a double membrane, cristae and 70S ribosomes: mitochondrion.

Example 3: plant cells lack centrioles; animal cells lack a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole.

10-mark exam-style question

(a) Describe the structure and function of the nucleus. [3]

(b) Outline how a protein for secretion is made and released, naming the organelles involved. [4]

(c) State three structural differences between a typical plant cell and a typical animal cell. [3]

Answers and mark guide:

  • (a) Surrounded by a double membrane (nuclear envelope) with pores (B1); contains chromatin/DNA, which carries the genetic code (B1); nucleolus makes ribosomes (rRNA) (B1).
  • (b) mRNA leaves the nucleus through nuclear pores (B1); the protein is made on ribosomes on the RER and moves through the RER (B1); vesicles carry it to the Golgi body, where it is modified and packaged (B1); secretory vesicles fuse with the cell surface membrane (exocytosis) (B1).
  • (c) Plants: cellulose cell wall; chloroplasts; large permanent vacuole; plasmodesmata; no centrioles (any three, B1 each).

Common mistakes

  1. Saying mitochondria "make energy" (they release energy / make ATP).
  2. Confusing RER (protein) with SER (lipid).
  3. Saying ribosomes are membrane-bound.
  4. Saying plant cells have no mitochondria.
  5. Calling the cell wall "the cell membrane".

Quick recall

  1. Site of aerobic respiration?
  2. Ribosome type in the cytoplasm of eukaryotes?
  3. Function of lysosomes?
  4. What do plasmodesmata do?
  5. Organelle that packages proteins?

Answers: 1) Mitochondrion. 2) 80S. 3) Contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down unwanted material. 4) Link the cytoplasm of neighbouring plant cells. 5) Golgi body.
